agree.reason: The candid opening and the 15% underlying growth figure would ease a cold investor somewhat, but the apology makes no commitment to future updates and there is no plan for the next raise, so they may stay wary.

honest.reason: Every number checks out against the brief ($35.5k to $41k, about 11 months of runway, 37 × $150 ≈ $5.5k), but 'records-system vendors are building their own schedulers' generalises from a single lost customer.

works_the_facts.reason: It derives runway, the 15% growth outside the lost chain, the near-halving of no-shows and the 37-customer break-even, each in its most favourable true form, though it doesn't work out the pace of reminder sales needed before cash runs out.

right_comparison.reason: It shows the underlying growth trend but never says what happens if nothing changes: with MRR flat and $44k a month burn, cash runs out around late 2027, before any fundraising timeline.

qualification.reason: The reminder launch and the 37-customer target have no date, no checkpoint number, and no stated consequence if they are missed, and runway is handed to investors as an open question.

objections.reason: It meets the missed-updates complaint and the 'is the business shrinking' worry, but leaves the resisting investor's main questions unanswered: will updates now arrive on time, when is the next round, and how fast can 37 reminder customers realistically be signed?

fit.reason: It's a clear, scannable investor email of about 370 words, well under the 500-word limit.
